title: Synchronous Callback Deadlock Coupling (The Observer Trap)
pattern: An event notifier executes user-registered callbacks synchronously while holding an internal lock or a read borrow on its own structure.
why_bad: It is a deadlock minefield. If the registered callback attempts to re-enter the event source, modify the registration list, or acquire a lock that the triggering thread holds, the system deadlocks.
detection: Methods that loop over a collection of traits or closures and execute them synchronously within a synchronized block or borrow scope.
counterexample: Purely functional map or transform callbacks (like `Iterator::map`) that run entirely on independent thread scopes.
fix:
Expose asynchronous callback triggers, execute callbacks outside the lock scope, or utilize an event queue that schedules callbacks to run on separate execution ticks.
```rust
// Execute callbacks after releasing the internal Mutex lock
```
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!* (2007), Chapter 4 ("Stability Anti-patterns - UserCallback.java").
